name: Steel Blue
lede: Steel blue is a mid, slightly greyed blue named for the cold sheen of the metal; on screens it is a CSS color, and in the paint trade it was a term for certain paler grades of Prussian blue.

sections.title: Two meanings
sections.body:
As a pigment term, steel blue was used for certain paler grades of [[prussian-blue]] [1]. Zerr and Rübencamp's early twentieth-century handbook suggests a trade split: iron blues with a metallic cast on the surface are bronze blue, and those without it are steel blue [2]. That cast, called bronzing, shows on particularly pure and densely applied Prussian blue [2].

Steel blue also appears in long lists of Prussian blue synonyms beside Paris blue, Milori blue and Chinese blue [1][3]. Paterson's dictionary describes the color as a greenish or greyish blue like steel, and notes it as another name for Prussian blue [4].

sections.title: The screen color
sections.body:
The swatch here is the web color `steelblue`, one of the 140 colors in the X11 set [4]. It is lighter and greyer than classic Prussian blue, which is a deep near-black blue [5]. Our library files it as an everyday color, and also lists it in ISCC-NBS block 172 and in Maerz & Paul, which dates the name to 1817 [5]. RAL 5011, a different industrial standard with the same name, is a far darker blue, so a swatch under this name can mean very different things [5].

Neighbors in the same family are [[cadet-blue]], [[sky-blue]] and [[cobalt-blue]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive, 41 of 23,781 paintings hold this blue [6]. John Singer Sargent shows it in 3 of his 287 works, about six times the archive rate [6]. Printed use of the words peaks around 1903 in Google Books [7]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a match is approximate and says nothing about which pigment was used [6].
